sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Den Haag has built its parking policy on resident permits and paid visitor parking. The Parkeerstrategie 2021–2030 limits the number of permits per area from 2022, creates extra spaces for residents in some neighbourhoods and investigates resident garages in old districts [0]. In September 2024 the city announced paid parking step by step in almost the whole city, no new third permit per household from 2025, and a ceiling per permit zone based on street spaces [1]. The 2026 regulation sets a ceiling on second and third permits where parking pressure is above 90%, with a waiting list by application date [2].

The street tariff is now the sharpest tool. After a trial of a flat €50 day rate in two areas lost customers for shopkeepers, the city replaced it from 1 April 2026 with a progressive tariff on 22 streets, 17 in the Old Centre and 5 in Scheveningen, from €0.35 a minute for the first 20 minutes up to a maximum of €50 beyond 90 minutes [4][5]. The main street rate is €2.75 an hour, and €7.15 in premium areas such as the central shopping streets [6]. Paid hours in the central zone run Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 24:00 and Sunday from 13:00 [7].

The politics have just shifted. A new coalition of Hart voor Den Haag, VVD, CDA and DENK presented its plans on 10 July 2026. The coalition says all planned expansions of paid parking except Houtwijk will not go ahead, and tariffs are to stay the same for the coming period apart from indexation [3]. A zero-emission zone for vans and lorries around the Centrumring was confirmed in June 2024 to start on 1 January 2025 [9], and the city's Netwerkstrategie 2040 expects traffic to fall by 4% and parking to happen more often in garages or at the city edge [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The centre's garage supply is being reshaped by works. The Spui garage is closed for the Spuikwartier renovation, and the Stadhuis garage stays open with its entrance moved to Ammunitiehaven [17]. The Turfmarktgarage is closed from September 2026 to February 2027, with Q-Park Spui, Stadhuis and Muzenplein listed as alternatives [16].

New housing areas are being planned with few cars. In Binckhorst the city applies a car-lite policy and issues no resident permits, and the municipality names Binckhorst, the Central Innovation District and Den Haag Zuidwest as low-car areas where permits are usually unavailable [12][13]. BinckPark, a planned public garage with 505 spaces, was shown in the plan-making phase on the city's page, modified in September 2026, with construction due to start in mid-2026 and completion in mid-2027, and the page does not confirm that construction has begun [14]. The park-and-ride sites include P+R Laan van NOI (155 spaces, run by Q-Park), Leidschenveen Haven, Ypenburg and Mariahoeve, which is free [22]. The city runs two automated garages, Noordwal Veenkade for subscribers and Apeldoornselaan, which is temporarily closed [23]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Garages in Den Haag are mostly run by Q-Park and Interparking. Our price list covers 69 garages, with Q-Park running 27, Interparking 9 and the rest listed through ParkBee with no capacity. Q-Park itself lists 23 facilities in the city [18]. Prices are highest near the Plein. Garages within 500 m have a median of €5.80 an hour, against €5.28 for those within 1 km, €3.59 at 1 to 2 km and €3.42 beyond 2 km. Garages near the centre cost about €5 an hour, well above the main street rate of €2.75 and below the premium €7.15: Q-Park's Centrum is €5.20, CS New Babylon €5.56 and the WTC (Interparking) €5.00. Out-of-centre garages such as Megastores cost €1.00 an hour.

The six car parks with measured occupancy hold 1,341 spaces, and averaged 32% on weekdays and 30% at weekends from August to early October 2026. Garage Helicon is the fullest (56% on weekdays, 50% at weekends), followed by the Pleingarage (38%), Markthof (35%) and Stadhuis (30%). The P+R Laan van NOI is at 17% and Binck City Park only 10%. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Den Haag.
